newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Senate derails move on church-run schools.
newsitem.headline: Canada Senate derails move on church-run schools.

text.p: The Canadian Senate on Wednesday derailed, temporarily at least, a government resolution to limit the power churches have over schools in the Atlantic province of Newfoundland.

The Senate, the unelected upper chamber of Parliament, changed the government's proposed amendment to the Canadian constitution that would have allowed the province to modify its church-run school system. The new version then passed.
Parliament's lower chamber, the elected House of Commons, in June voted massively in favour of the constitutional change, which had already been approved by Newfoundland.

Canadian Justice Minister Allan Rock said immediately afterward that the original amendment would be reintroduced in the near future in the House, which has the power to override the Senate vote. But the process could take time.

Newfoundland's schools are run on denominational lines with 27 separate school boards. The constitutional amendment would have allowed the provincial government to eliminate school boards, merge schools and bus students to the nearest school rather than the school of the student's choice.
Opposition to the bill stemmed from concern about the possibility of Roman Catholic schools in other provinces losing their funding if a precedent were set.
"(The amendment) would create a dangerous precedent," said Conservative Sen. John Lynch-Staunton in a statement before the vote.
The version passed by the Senate provided for denominational schools continuing "where numbers warrant," to protect religous minorities.
The denominational nature of the province's education which was guaranteed in the terms under which Newfoundland joined Canada in 1949.
